newsitem.title: INDIA: India coalition party in talks on joining government.
newsitem.headline: India coalition party in talks on joining government.

text.p: A key regional party in India's United Front alliance began a crucial executive meeting on Sunday to decide whether to join Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's government that assumed office last week.

"The committee will decide, taking into account the national interests," Jayanthi Natarajan, general secretary of the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC), told reporters as she went in for the meeting in Madras, capital of the southern state of Tamil Nadu.

TMC's decision, expected later on Sunday, was keenly awaited by investors as one of the party's leader, P. Chidambaram, is a key economic reform architect who as finance minister presented a tax-cutting budget for 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28.
Gujral has not appointed a finance minister in his cabinet, signalling the slot was open for Chidambaram.
The TMC, a member of the previous United Front government under H.D. Deve Gowda, did not join Gujral's coalition because its president, G.K. Moopanar, lost the race to become premier.
The Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), pushed for a prime minister from northern Indian, saying there was a need to check the Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in its stronghold.
But this was seen by analysts and newspapers as a move to check Moopanar because of his closeness to the Congress party.
The TMC was formed last year by Congress defectors upset with their leadership over a regional electoral alliance.
It has 20 of the 177 alliance lawmakers in the 545-member lower house, the Lok Sabha. The CPI-M has 32. Neither of them is represented in the government.
